thread:
maya: Heads up — importing the JS SDK (v0.9.1) in a Cloudflare Worker throws a runtime ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined.
ryan: Oof. Can you paste the exact import and the error stack?
maya: Sure, here's the root import and the error:```js
import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-js';
// worker startup -> ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined
    at Object.<anonymous> (dist/index.cjs:12:15)
    at __webpack_require__ (bootstrap.js:19:0)
```
tomas: Sounds like the published bundle leaks Node Buffer usage (or a CJS-compiled lib that requires('buffer')). CF Workers don't provide Node globals. The SDK needs a browser/edge build.
maya: Our build pipeline currently outputs a CJS bundle as main and an ESM under module, but the CJS still contains `require('buffer')` fallback. Also seeing a TS error in a TS worker project: "Could not find a declaration file for module 'redwood-js'" — typings aren't exposing the edge entry.
benji: Short-term options: polyfill Buffer in the worker entrypoint (globalThis.Buffer = globalThis.Buffer || Uint8Array) or import buffer/ponyfill, but both add bytes and are hacky. Better: publish a browser-friendly ESM build and proper conditional exports.
ryan: Agreed. We can add a conditional exports map in package.json. Example snippet:```json
{
  "exports": {
    "./package.json": "./package.json",
    "./edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
}
```
That lets users `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-js/edge'` or bundlers to pick import/require.
maya: Trying `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-js/edge'` locally — that fixed the Buffer error after edge build. But bundlers still resolve to the CJS main if they don't prefer 'import' field.
tomas: We should also ship a top-level `browser`/`module` field and ensure `exports.import` points to an ESM browser build. For typings, include a separate types file for edge that uses lib.dom instead of node types to avoid Node-specific types bleeding into public API.
benji: For TypeScript: add a dist/types/edge.d.ts and in package.json `exports: { "./edge": { "types": "./dist/types/edge.d.ts", "default": "./dist/edge/index.mjs" } }` — keeps things tidy. Also update tsconfig for the edge build to include "lib": ["es2020", "dom"] so DOM types are available.
devex-bot: npm: published redwood-js@0.9.2-edge-candidate to tag 'edge-candidate' (build+types updated).
maya: Confirmed the candidate works in my CF Worker without polyfills. Types auto-resolve in VSCode when importing from 'redwood-js/edge'.
ryan: Great. Follow-ups: (1) add CLI docs about `-edge` import for workers, (2) long-term: make conditional exports resolve automatically so users don't need explicit '/edge' path, (3) add test job that runs the ESM edge bundle in a lightweight worker runtime.
tomas: I'll open a PR to change build pipeline to produce edge artifacts + update package.json exports and add the TS edge types.
benji: Also add a short onboarding note in Quickstarts: "If you're targeting Cloudflare Workers or other edge runtime, import from 'redwood-js/edge'" until auto-resolve is solid.
maya: Thanks y'all — this was blocking an onboarding flow. :relieved:
ryan: :thumbsup: tagging @devex to track the backlog task.
